items.stem: Farmers of a village near Chandigarh join together to use tractors and better seeds on their combined land. Identify the type of cooperative society. Justify your answer.
items.answer: Farmer's cooperative society. Benefits of large-scale farming.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Farmer's cooperative society; 2 marks for the justification: Benefits of large-scale farming.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of partnership but not of joint stock company?
items.answer: Transfer of interest: not possible without consent of all partners
items.markingKey: (d) partnership: Transfer of interest: not possible without consent of all partners. The other options describe joint stock company.
options: Transfer of interest: shares of a public company freely transferable
Transfer of interest: not possible without consent of all partners

items.stem: All partners of Patel Stores have unlimited liability and all take part in management. Identify the type of partnership. Justify your answer.
items.answer: General partnership. Unlimited liability of all partners.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying General partnership; 2 marks for the justification: Unlimited liability of all partners.

items.stem:
Harleen wants to start a technology venture alone but also wants limited liability and the ability to bring in investors later.
(i) Which form can she use now? State its main feature. (ii) What form may she move to as investors join, and why? (iii) Give one difference between a private and a public company relevant to her.
items.answer: (i) A One Person Company: a company with a single member and limited liability. (ii) A private company (minimum two members, up to 200), and later a public company to raise funds from the public. (iii) A private company cannot invite the public and restricts share transfer; a public company can invite the public and shares are freely transferable.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) A One Person Company: a company with a single member and limited liability. (ii) A private company (minimum two members, up to 200), and later a public company to raise funds from the public. (iii) A private company cannot invite the public and restricts share transfer; a public company can invite the public and shares are freely transferable.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of sole proprietorship but not of partnership?
items.answer: Risk: borne by the proprietor alone
items.markingKey: (b) sole proprietorship: Risk: borne by the proprietor alone. The other options describe partnership.
options: Formation: formed by an agreement among partners
Risk: borne by the proprietor alone

items.stem: Fifty milk producers of a village near Patna want to sell their milk together and serve their own interests rather than earn profit. Which form of business organisation is most suitable? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Cooperative society. Service motive and pooling by producers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Cooperative society; 2 marks for the justification: Service motive and pooling by producers.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Marketing cooperative society"?
items.answer: Set up to help small producers sell their products by pooling their output and selling it at the best price.
items.markingKey: (d) Marketing cooperative society: Set up to help small producers sell their products by pooling their output and selling it at the best price.
options: Provides loans to members at low rates of interest and protects them from money lenders.
Set up to protect small producers by supplying raw materials, equipment and other inputs.
Formed to protect the interests of consumers by buying in bulk and selling to members at reasonable prices, eliminating middlemen.
Set up to help small producers sell their products by pooling their output and selling it at the best price.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the choice of form of organisation is correct?
items.answer: Sole proprietorship is the easiest form to set up.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: Sole proprietorship is the easiest form to set up.
options: A partnership provides limited liability to all partners.
A sole proprietorship is best for raising very large capital.
Degree of control has no bearing on the choice of form.
Sole proprietorship is the easiest form to set up.

items.stem: Identify the type of cooperative society. In each case give a reason. (i) Residents of a colony in Nagpur form a society to buy groceries in bulk and sell them to members at fair prices. (ii) Small dairy farmers of Nagpur pool their milk and sell it through their society at the best price.
items.answer: (i) Consumer's cooperative society: It protects consumers and removes middlemen. (ii) Marketing cooperative society: It helps producers sell by pooling output.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Consumer's cooperative society (ii) Marketing cooperative society

items.stem: Farhan runs a small stationery shop in Mumbai alone, takes all decisions and keeps all profits. (i) Identify the form of business organisation. (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Sole proprietorship: One person owns, manages and bears all risk. (ii) Any two of: owned and controlled by one person; unlimited liability; easy formation and closure; no separate legal entity; lack of business continuity
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: owned and controlled by one person; unlimited liability; easy formation and closure; no separate legal entity; lack of business continuity
